Pokémon 30th Anniversary Cards: Full Card List & Prices

2026-10-10 · Updated 2026-11-16

English 30th Celebration has 161 main-set/RGB cards and a separate 30-card Classic Collection: 191 cards across those two groups. Below are both complete lists with their published USD price references. For example, Mew ex 152/128 was $54.54 and Classic Collection Charizard 4/102 was $109.63 on November 15, 2026.

Sources: the official Pokémon checklist, official gallery and CardScanFox’s main-set and Classic Collection catalogs, checked November 15, 2026; each row retains its own price observation date.

158 numbered cards · 3 RGB Mew cards · 30 Classic Collection cards · Identify your card · How to get the cards

Which cards count toward the set?

English checklist groups
GroupCountNumbering
Main numbered expansion158001/128–158/128
RGB Rare Mew3R/RGB, G/RGB, B/RGB
Classic Collection30Original-style card numbers
Total in the tables below191Excludes Basic Energy and product promos

The printed denominator 128 is the main numbered set size. Cards 129/128–158/128 extend beyond it. The 30 different Pikachu illustrations are numbered 023/128–052/128. The official PDF also lists eight foil Basic Energy cards; those and product promos are outside the 191-card checklist below. Its numbered list does not show the three RGB Mew identifiers, which are listed in the public catalog.

The price columns show the catalog’s selected raw-card reference for an English printing. Open a card to see its source, condition and finish, or select an existing slab grade. The price methodology explains the reference selection.

How to identify your anniversary card

  1. Read the full collector number at the bottom of the card. A number such as 152/128 belongs to the main 30C list; R/RGB, G/RGB and B/RGB identify the three Mew colors.
  2. For a Classic Collection card such as Charizard 4/102, match the anniversary marking, artwork and 30C-CC release. The older Base Set card uses the same number.
  3. Confirm the language and finish, then open the linked card record for the price context that matches your copy.

Browse the Pokémon hub for other sets. With a card in hand, use the Pokémon card scanner and confirm the suggested printing.

How to get Pokémon 30th Anniversary cards

Buy a single when you want one exact printing

Use the number, language, artwork and finish in the tables above to identify the card you want. Compare a seller's front and back photos with that printing, then check the stated raw condition or existing slab grade. The table's dated raw-card reference helps compare that record; use the seller's checkout for the actual asking price, delivery cost and availability.

Choose booster packs for randomized cards

Regular 30th Celebration packs and Classic Collection packs belong to different groups. Check the product description before buying: the three-card Classic Collection pack is separate from a regular expansion pack. Buying random packs does not select a particular numbered card; start with a single when your goal is one missing checklist entry.

Choose a Day or Night UPC for its fixed promos and accessories

The Day collection pairs Pikachu ex with Espeon ex; Night pairs Pikachu ex with Umbreon ex. Use the UPC contents and Day vs Night guide to compare the included promos, 29 regular boosters, one Classic Collection booster and accessories. The fixed promos are different from the random pack pulls.

For sealed products, use the official Pokémon TCG retailer directory and confirm the selected product in your region. For singles, keep the set and complete number in the seller search. Return to the Pokémon card price database for another printing or use the Pokémon scanner to identify a card you already own.

UPC box contents and Day vs Night

For the sealed product, use the separate 30th Anniversary UPC Day and Night guide. It covers the November 6 release, two promo pairings, pack counts, accessories and retailer information.

Questions

Is 30th Celebration the same as the 2021 Celebrations set?

No. This list covers the 2026 English 30C expansion and 30C-CC reprints. The 2021 Celebrations release has its own checklist.

Why do I see 158, 161 or 191 cards on different lists?

158 counts the numbered expansion cards. Add three RGB Mew cards for 161. Add the 30 Classic Collection reprints for 191. Basic Energy, product promos and additional print variants change the scope again.

Do these prices apply to graded cards?

The tables use raw-card references. For an existing slab, select its grading company and grade on the linked record. Read the raw vs graded guide for the difference.
